head: A holiday with no cash,
no clocks, no worries.
slides.sub: How Club Med invented a new way to vacation, then had to reinvent itself.

image.label: Canvas tents on a Mediterranean beach at sunrise
image.brief: 1950년대 지중해 해변의 해 뜰 무렵, 줄지어 선 낡은 캔버스 텐트들. 따뜻한 필름 톤. 로고 없음.

head: 1950. A beach in Mallorca.
A village made of tents.
body: Gérard Blitz, a Belgian former water polo player, set up a holiday camp in Alcúdia, Spain, using surplus army tents. Guests slept on the sand, cooked together and swam all day.
Europe was still recovering from war. Cheap, simple escape was exactly what people wanted.

image.label: Young people eating at a long table beside tents
image.brief: 전후 1950년대 분위기, 텐트 옆 긴 나무 식탁에서 함께 식사하는 젊은이들의 실루엣. 인물 얼굴은 특정하지 않음.

head: One price paid
for everything.
body: Guests paid once and stopped thinking about money. At the bar, they paid with plastic beads worn as a necklace. Staff were called G.O.s, gentle organizers, and guests were G.M.s, gentle members.
Staff ate, played and danced with guests. The holiday felt like joining a club.

image.label: A necklace of colorful plastic beads on a bar counter
image.brief: 해변 바 카운터 위에 놓인 알록달록한 플라스틱 구슬 목걸이. 1960년대 색감.

head: From tents
to a global brand.
body: Gilbert Trigano, who had supplied the tents, joined and ran the company for decades. Straw huts became villages, then ski resorts and beach resorts far beyond Europe.
Club Med went public in Paris in the 1960s. Its name became shorthand for the all-inclusive holiday.

image.label: A vintage map dotted with resort pins
image.brief: 전 세계 휴양지에 핀이 꽂힌 빈티지 지도. 지중해, 알프스, 카리브해 등. 실제 로고 없음.

head: Everyone copied the idea.
The magic faded.
body: By the 1990s, rivals sold all-inclusive packages too, often cheaper. Many Club Med villages looked dated, and the company was losing money.
In 1997, the founding Trigano family left management. Club Med needed to decide what it stood for.

image.label: A tired resort pool with faded loungers
image.brief: 1990년대 빛바랜 선베드가 놓인 한산한 리조트 수영장. 약간 쓸쓸한 톤.

head: Rivals sell your idea cheaper.
What do you do?
body: It's the early 2000s. You invented the all-inclusive holiday, but now it's everywhere and your villages are aging.

options.text: Go upmarket: close cheap villages and target well-off families
options.feedback: This means fewer guests and closing places loyal fans love. Keep swiping.

options.text: Cut prices to fill every bed and win back volume
options.feedback: Full villages feel good, but you'd be fighting rivals with lower costs on their terms. Keep swiping.

options.text: Keep the formula and refresh the marketing
options.feedback: Cheaper than rebuilding, but the product itself was the problem. Keep swiping.

image.label: A crossroads sign on a tropical beach path
image.brief: 열대 해변 길 위의 갈림길 표지판. 한쪽은 고급 리조트, 한쪽은 붐비는 해변.

head: Fewer villages.
Higher prices.
body: Under Henri Giscard d'Estaing, Club Med chose to move upmarket. It closed or sold many basic villages and rebuilt others for comfort, with kids' clubs and better food.
The old party crowd drifted away. Families with money came in.

image.label: A modern upscale resort with a family by the pool
image.brief: 현대적인 고급 리조트, 수영장 옆 가족의 뒷모습 실루엣. 밝고 세련된 톤.

slides.label: resorts today, down from more than 100 at the peak
body: Club Med became smaller but more premium. In 2015, after a long takeover battle, China's Fosun bought the company, betting on growing demand from Chinese travelers.

image.label: A snowy mountain resort lit up at night
image.brief: 밤에 불 밝힌 눈 덮인 산악 리조트. 아시아 관광객 분위기 암시, 얼굴 없음.

head: It survived.
It no longer owned the idea.
body: The all-inclusive holiday Club Med invented is now sold by countless hotel chains. Club Med lived on, but as one premium brand among many.
The invention spread. The company had to compete on something else.

image.label: Many resort towers along a crowded coastline
image.brief: 해안선을 따라 빽빽이 들어선 여러 리조트 건물. 원조 빌리지가 작게 보이는 구도.

head: Inventing a category
doesn't mean owning it.
body: Club Med created a new category, but an idea like one price for everything is easy to copy. Once rivals did, the edge eroded and price became the battleground.
Moving upmarket meant competing on experience and brand, not on being first.

image.label: A bead necklace dissolving into many copies
image.brief: 구슬 목걸이 하나가 여러 개의 복제품으로 퍼져 나가는 그래픽.

head: Your first idea gets copied.
Plan your second edge.
body: Being first wins attention. Staying ahead takes something rivals can't easily copy.
**Try it today:** if a competitor copied your best feature tomorrow, why would customers still choose you?

image.label: A single tent on an empty beach at dusk
image.brief: 해 질 녘 텅 빈 해변 위 텐트 하나.

factChecks.note: 1950년 Gérard Blitz가 스페인 마요르카 알쿠디아에서 군용 잉여 텐트로 첫 빌리지를 연 것과 Gilbert Trigano가 텐트 공급자로 참여한 이야기는 Club Med 공식 연혁 기준입니다. 텐트 출처(미군 잉여품)는 자료마다 표현이 다르니 확인하세요.
현금 대신 쓰던 구슬 목걸이(pop beads)와 G.O.(gentils organisateurs)·G.M.(gentils membres) 호칭은 널리 기록된 사실입니다. 도입 시기는 단정하지 않았습니다.
Gilbert Trigano가 수십 년간 회사를 이끌고, 1990년대 손실 뒤 1997년 Trigano 가문이 경영에서 물러난(Serge Trigano 퇴진) 과정은 Le Monde, Financial Times 등 당시 보도로 확인하세요.
Henri Giscard d'Estaing 체제에서 2000년대 초중반 고급화 전략으로 저가 빌리지를 닫은 사실은 회사 발표와 보도 기준입니다. 정확한 시작 연도(2002 CEO 취임, 2004년 무렵 전략 발표)는 확인하세요.
"약 70개 리조트"는 최근 회사 자료 기준의 대략적 수치입니다. 연도에 따라 60~80개 사이로 달라지므로 최신 자료로 확인하고, 피크 시 100개 이상이었다는 표현도 함께 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 현재 약 70개, 피크 100개 이상은 이번 검색에서 미확인.

Fosun이 Investindustrial과의 2년 가까운 인수 경쟁 끝에 2015년 Club Med를 인수한 사실은 Reuters 등 보도 기준입니다. 인수 금액(약 9억 4천만 유로 보도)은 카드에 넣지 않았습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] Fosun과 Investindustrial의 2013~2015년 인수 경쟁, 2015년 초 Fosun 컨소시엄 승리 확인.
